transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Cassiopeia CTO), Jenna (ML Eng), Samuel (SRE), Lina (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, keep as rough):
- Demo focused on JSON-mode structured outputs and tool-calling to drive a search + db enrichment pipeline.
- Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a pilot; security and latency are key constraints.
- Agreed next steps: pricing + pilot docs, schema templates, and perf benchmark.

Topics: JSON mode, schemas, guardrails, function/tool calling, Redwood Console, Optimize suggestions, VPC/private deployment considerations.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: all right thanks everyone for joining, uh i'm alex from redwood inference, i'll kick us off then priya will walk through the console and a live api demo. quick check, everyone can hear ok?
[00:18] Mark: yep loud and clear, thanks alex.
[00:22] Priya: great — hi team, excited to walk through JSON-mode and how we typically wire tool calls for enrichment and deterministic outputs. just a heads up the demo uses a small dataset and a schema we prepared.
[00:36] Jenna: quick context — our main flow is: user query -> retrieval -> llm extract structured candidate -> enrichment via internal db + external search, we'd like to guarantee shape of the response for downstream systems.
[00:52] Priya: that exactly maps to json mode, where you can pin a schema and return typed fields. we'll also show tool/function calling pattern for the enrichment step so you can keep the model's role surface area minimal.
[01:08] Samuel: latency target is sub-300 ms 95 for the extraction step, we can tolerate more for enrichment if it's async — cost is also a big factor, we don't want to pay 3x for everything.
[01:24] Alex: understood, okay we'll show how batching and caching in Optimize reduce token cost, and also how dedicated capacity gives predictable latency.
[01:31] Priya: jumping into the console, this is the 'structured-output' demo workspace — note the schema on screen: {title:string, product_id:int, confidence:float, attributes:array}. the console validates responses against this schema and can auto-fallback to a post-processing step if validation fails, so you get deterministic downstream behavior. (link to demo deck: https://app.redwood/demo-deck-cassiopeia)
[01:58] Jenna: does the validation run in-line or after streaming? we need streaming for UX.
[02:05] Priya: streaming still works — we validate on chunks and you can get partial output; final validation happens at the end, and we have a 'soft-fail' mode which sends a structured error object instead of raw text.
[02:20] Mark: about tool calling — can we call our internal product catalog search (REST) and also enrich results with a db read? how does auth work?
[02:32] Priya: yes, typically you'll register an external tool in the private control plane with a service account token. for private deployments you can use the VPC connector and we support vault-backed keys or customer KMS/HSM for credentials. we also record the tool invocation in the audit log for SOC 2 / ISO purposes.
[02:48] Samuel: cool, how about SSO for ops team?
[02:51] Alex: we have SAML/SSO integration, role-based access control, and token scoping per route. we'll share the security whitepaper after.
[03:01] Priya: switching to API mode: here's a sample request using json_mode=true plus a schema payload. the model returns structured json, and then we show the 'tool_call' field — if present the runtime pauses and invokes the registered tool, returns the tool output back into the model input for a second pass. it's configurable: synchronous call or queued async.
[03:28] Jenna: i saw an example where the runtime did a fallback to a smaller quantized model if the primary was busy — will that change output shape?
[03:36] Priya: good call — we have compatibility checks on model variants. if the fallback model can't reliably produce the exact schema we set a transform to normalize outputs or we run the validation post-hoc and route to a safe human-review queue. you can set a hard SLO to avoid falling back automatically.
[03:55] Mark: what about telemetry — we need token-level cost per request to map to our feature usage.
[04:02] Alex: Console shows token breakdown per-route, and Optimize will surface suggestions like increasing batch window or enabling prefix cache for very repeated prompts to cut cost.
[04:12] Priya: demo time — i'll run a live endpoint call. (typing noises) request sent: {prompt:..., json_mode:true, schema:..., tools:[catalog_search, db_read]}.
[04:28] Speaker 1 (auto): [inaudible]
[04:33] Priya: okay first pass returned a structured object with items[0] product_id 8923, confidence 0.94. tool_call asked for catalog_search with query 'best lightweight router' — runtime invoked the registered tool, returned 3 matches, model then merged attributes and returned final json.
[04:55] Jenna: that flow looks clean. a few practical q's: how do we test schema changes without breaking prod?
[05:05] Priya: we support versioned schemas and can do canary rollouts — you can pin a route to old schema v1 and route 10% of traffic to v2. there's also an eval harness in the console where you can run your prompt set against a new schema to surface regressions.
[05:23] Mark: how much effort to onboard? our infra team will want to review network flows and the VPC peering.
[05:30] Alex: typical pilot (4–6 weeks) — week 1 integration and schema/samples, week 2 perf bench, weeks 3–4 iterating guardrails and runbook, then extend to a small prod canary. we can do hosted pilot or dedicated depending on traffic.
[05:46] Samuel: dedicated seems safer for us because of noise and predictable p95, but we want to validate cost delta. can you show a cost comparison?
[05:54] Alex: yes we'll attach a cost model spreadsheet comparing hosted vs dedicated with the same workload — that'll be included in the pricing email.
[06:03] Jenna: what about retries/fallbacks when a tool times out? we can't have partial enrichment silently drop.
[06:10] Priya: we expose retry policies per-tool; if a tool times out you can choose fallback strategies — return partial structured object with 'enrichment_status:delayed' or route the request through an async worker and send webhooks on completion. all of that is configurable in the route settings.
[06:29] Mark: any constraints on schema complexity? nested arrays with variable length?
[06:35] Priya: complex schemas are supported — we recommend keeping critical fields at the top level and bounding arrays (maxItems) to avoid surprises; Optimize will flag prompts that frequently violate array bounds.
[06:49] Speaker 2: [crosstalk]
[06:54] Priya: demo — switching to the Optimize tab: here's a recommendation to change batch_size from 8 to 16 with prefix caching on the KV store; for your prompt distribution (lots of similar prefix queries) this can cut token cost by ~30% without increasing observed p95. we also surfaced quantization suggestion: int8 for latent models, but for the extraction step we recommend fp16 on a smaller model to hit the 300ms target.
[07:21] Jenna: do you measure quality drift after quantization?
[07:24] Priya: yes — we run evals attached to prompt sets and have regression alerts. you can set thresholds for acceptable quality drop and block automatic quantization if an eval fails.
[07:33] Samuel: security question again — are tool creds stored in Redwood or can we keep them in our vault?
[07:39] Alex: you can keep creds in your vault and use short-lived tokens or bring-your-own-kms. for on-prem or air-gapped deployments we can ship a private control plane.
[07:48] Mark: okay that helps, thank you.
[07:52] Priya: small hiccup — the live demo produced a slightly malformed number for product_id (model spit a string). you'll see validation triggered and the runtime emitted a 'validation_error' object. let me toggle the soft-fix post-process (demo).
[08:11] Priya: post-process fixed it to int by casting when safe, and left a warning in the audit log. this is configurable — some customers prefer hard rejects.
[08:23] Jenna: nice, we need the audit log for devops, can we stream audit events to our SIEM?
[08:30] Alex: yep syslog, forwarder, or cloud event bridge integrations supported.
[08:35] Mark: quick procurement note — we have to complete a security questionnaire and provide data residency requirements.
[08:41] Alex: we'll send over the security packet and SOC2 artifacts. also we can record region preference during pilot provisioning.
[08:49] Lina: product question — if we switch schema while retaining older customers, can we have the API return both v1 and v2 shapes?
[08:56] Priya: you can enable multi-schema responses: the runtime can return a compatibility wrapper with both shapes or serve a transform to map v2->v1 for legacy consumers. we showed an example in the deck.
[09:08] Speaker 3: [laughs]
[09:11] Priya: wrapping up demo — key takeaways: schema-anchored outputs for deterministic downstreams, function/tool calling for enrichment with audit trail, and Optimize to tunecost/latency tradeoffs.
[09:25] Alex: now open floor for questions and then we'll recap next steps.
[09:30] Mark: two more questions — 1) bench: can you run a 10k request perf test? 2) fallback human review: what's the UX for that?
[09:40] Priya: 1) yes we can run 10k bench on a dedicated pool — we'll need the sample prompt set and expected concurrency. 2) human-review: you can configure a human-review queue in console, integrates with Slack/email and you get annotated json with diff highlighting.
[09:58] Jenna: one more technical — how does KV caching interact with retrieval? we have a big vector db but repeated prefix extracts could be cached.
[10:06] Priya: KV prefix cache stores the model key-value states for repeated context sequences; for retrievals we recommend hybrid approach: cache frequent retrievals then enrich with vector db when needed. Optimize will recommend which items to cache based on LRU and observed reuse.
[10:23] Samuel: latency request again: can we see p95 over time in dashboard?
[10:28] Alex: yes, console has per-route p50/p95/p99 plus token cost; you can also set alerts.
[10:33] Mark: thanks, that's very helpful.
[10:36] Priya: final quick note — we'll provide schema examples (simple, nested, and long-array) and a postman/cli collection so your infra team can replicate calls locally.
[10:47] Alex: great, to recap next steps: i'll send pricing + pilot contract, priya will share schema templates and recorded walkthrough, samuel/mark to send infra details and prompt sets, then we schedule the perf bench.
[11:02] Mark: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:05] Jenna: thank you.
[11:07] End meeting.
